To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) DPPs are a natural and principled approach for minibatch sampling; (ii) DPPs can reduce the variance of gradient estimators, and hence the convergence rate, of SGD; (iii) the variance of DPP gradient estimators can be reduced by exploiting the specific data distribution via orthogonal polynomials; and (iv) DPPs and orthogonal polynomials enable efficient minibatch sampling and gradient estimation in SGD.

we introduce and analyse an orthogonal polynomial-based DPP paradigm for minibatch sampling in stochastic gradient descent, and that this approach leads to gradient estimators that converge faster than under uniform sampling.
we provide a new DPP-based minibatch construction method for SGD that is based on orthogonal polynomails and that we provide a detailed theoretical analysis and empirical validation of this method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, analysis, and implementation of minibatch construction methods for SGD.
the problem of constructing minibatches for SGD in a way that is both principled and efficient, and provides theoretical guarantees for a wide range of machine learning problems.
the following questions. How to construct minibatches for SGD that are more effective in terms of variance than uniform sampling, while being easy to sample?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DPP-based sampling of minibatches in SGD leads to a better trade-off between variance and computational cost.
our method leads to faster SGD convergence, with less variance, less computational overhead and less bias than uniform minibatching.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for SGD on a convex objective, our DPP-based minibatch sampling scheme can lead to a faster convergence rate than uniform sampling.
, for SGD on convex loss minimization, our orthogonal polynomial-based DPP minibatch paradigm is the first principled approach that can lead to a faster rate of convergence than uniform sampling.
, for a given data set and SGD algorithm, DPP minibatch sampling can be a powerful and practical tool to improve the variance of the gradient estimator.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for SGD on convex losses, DPP minibatch sampling leads to a smaller bound of the mean square approximation of the gradient, which translates into faster convergence of SGD, as compared to uniform sampling.
DPPs are not just an interesting mathematical object, but can also be a powerful tool for machine learning.
, for SGD, DPPs are not merely a tool to construct diverse minibatches but also to reduce the variance of the gradient estimator.
